Uses database transaction listeners to stage and apply descriptor re-encryptions, ensures descriptor plaintext key erasures succeed within an atomic transaction, and removes deliberate process aborts (`assert(false)`) on failed encryption commits. Replaces boolean return values in wallet unlock and passphrase change interfaces with `util::Expected<void, WalletError>`, allowing callers to distinguish between incorrect passphrases and database or encryption write failures.",

A failed encryption commit crashes the node with an assertion failure; a failed passphrase write leaves the new passphrase active only in memory until restart; and a failed descriptor key write or erase can either publish unpersisted keys or leave plaintext keys on disk. Additionally, boolean returns force RPC and GUI callers to misreport database errors as incorrect passphrases.",

result.summary: Makes wallet encryption, passphrase changes, and descriptor key additions atomic by updating in-memory key state only after database writes and commits succeed. Uses database transaction listeners to stage and apply descriptor re-encryptions, ensures descriptor plaintext key erasures succeed within an atomic transaction, and removes deliberate process aborts (`assert(false)`) on failed encryption commits. Replaces boolean return values in wallet unlock and passphrase change interfaces with `util::Expected<void, WalletError>`, allowing callers to distinguish between incorrect passphrases and database or encryption write failures.
result.problem: Database write or commit failures during wallet encryption, key insertion, or passphrase changes leave disk records and in-memory key state out of sync. A failed encryption commit crashes the node with an assertion failure; a failed passphrase write leaves the new passphrase active only in memory until restart; and a failed descriptor key write or erase can either publish unpersisted keys or leave plaintext keys on disk. Additionally, boolean returns force RPC and GUI callers to misreport database errors as incorrect passphrases.
evidence: Commit 8b23fa4773 and src/wallet/wallet.cpp show that failed encryption transactions previously hit `assert(false)`: '// We now probably have half of our keys encrypted in memory, and half not... die and let the user reload the unencrypted wallet.'

PR description notes: 'Encryption can report success without persisting the master key, and a passphrase change can activate the new passphrase only in memory... A failed encryption transaction commit aborts the node, and a re-encryption failure during a passphrase change can leave a previously locked wallet unlocked.'
result.scope_notes: Adds a reusable `FaultInjectingDatabase` test utility to simulate SQLite write, erase, and commit failures.
result.card: This PR makes wallet encryption, descriptor key additions, and passphrase changes atomic, ensuring in-memory key state is updated only after database transactions commit. Currently, database write or commit failures during these operations can leave in-memory keys out of sync with disk, leave plaintext keys on disk after encryption, leave a locked wallet unlocked on re-encryption failure, or trigger a hard process abort via assert(false). The changes also convert wallet unlock and passphrase modification methods to return structured errors, preventing database write failures from being misreported to RPC and GUI users as incorrect passphrases. It includes characterization and fault-injection unit tests covering database write, erase, and commit failures.
